events.title: Iran Demands Greater Oil Revenue from Anglo-Iranian Oil Company
events.note: Razmara pressed for 50-50 arrangement starting 1950; the AIOC's refusal drove the nationalization movement. Well documented.

events.title: National Front Gains Parliamentary Influence
events.note: Mosaddegh's National Front made gains in the 16th Majlis (1950 elections); platform was oil nationalization. Confirmed.

events.title: Assassination of Prime Minister Razmara
events.note: Razmara assassinated March 7, 1951 by Khalil Tahmasebi of Fadayan-e Islam. Date and perpetrator confirmed.

events.title: Oil Nationalization and Mosaddegh Becomes Prime Minister
events.note: Nationalization law passed March 15-17 1951; Mosaddegh appointed PM April 28, 1951. Date matches sources exactly.

events.title: International Court of Justice Dispute Over Oil Nationalization
events.note: Britain filed at ICJ and UNSC; Mosaddegh argued in person; ICJ ruled it lacked jurisdiction July 1952. Confirmed.

events.title: July Uprising (30 Tir) Restores Mosaddegh
events.note: July 21 1952 (30 Tir). Shah appointed Qavam; mass protests forced reinstatement of Mosaddegh. Dozens killed. Confirmed.

events.title: Britain Breaks Diplomatic Relations with Iran
events.note: Diplomatic break October 1952 after Iran expelled British embassy staff. Confirmed.

events.title: CIA-MI6 Coup Overthrows Mosaddegh (Operation AJAX/Boot)
events.note: August 19, 1953. CIA (AJAX/TP-AJAX) and MI6 (Boot) confirmed. Shah had fled to Rome; paid mobs deployed. ~300 killed. CIA declassified documents confirm. Exact date confirmed.

events.title: Shah Returns from Exile and Consolidates Power
events.note: Shah returned August 22, 1953 from Rome (not Baghdad as sometimes stated). Zahedi appointed PM. Confirmed.

events.title: Oil Consortium Agreement Ends Nationalization in Practice
events.note: Consortium agreement signed August 1954. 50% to Iran, Western companies retained operational control. British boycott ended. Confirmed.

events.title: Tudeh Party Purged from Military
events.note: Post-coup purge of Tudeh from military well documented; hundreds arrested, executed, or imprisoned 1953-54. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Joins Baghdad Pact (CENTO)
events.note: Iran joined Baghdad Pact November 1955 (UK, Turkey, Iraq, Pakistan already members). Confirmed.

events.title: Anti-Baha'i Pogroms
events.note: 1955 anti-Baha'i campaign; Falsafi sermons broadcast on state radio; Baha'i HQ in Tehran attacked. Confirmed.

events.title: SAVAK Secret Police Established
events.note: SAVAK formally established March 1957 (some sources say 1956 for the authorizing decree). CIA and Mossad assistance confirmed. Minor year ambiguity but event is real.

events.title: Iran Expands Ties with Israel Despite Arab Opposition
events.note: Israel-Iran de facto relations from mid-1950s; intelligence cooperation and oil supply confirmed. Not publicly announced but well documented historically.

events.title: US-Iran Bilateral Defense Agreement
events.note: US-Iran bilateral defense agreement 1957 confirmed; part of Eisenhower Doctrine regional security architecture. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran's First Nuclear Research Reactor Agreement with US
events.note: Atoms for Peace agreement 1957; Tehran Research Reactor (5 MW) became operational 1967. Dates confirmed.

events.title: Iraqi Revolution Alarms the Shah
events.note: July 14, 1958 Iraqi coup killed Faisal II; shocked Tehran and accelerated US-Iran security cooperation. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Signs Bilateral Security Agreement with the United States
events.note: March 5, 1959 bilateral security agreement following Iraq's withdrawal from Baghdad Pact. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Claims Bahrain as Its 14th Province
events.note: Iran's formal claim to Bahrain as 14th province pre-dates 1959 but was reasserted in this period. UN plebiscite 1970 confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Second National Front and Political Unrest
events.note: Second National Front re-emerged ~1960; student protests at Tehran University; Shah dissolved parliament. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Becomes OPEC Founding Member
events.note: OPEC founded September 1960 in Baghdad; Iran one of five founding members (Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Venezuela). Confirmed.

events.title: Ali Amini Appointed Prime Minister; Pressure for Reform
events.note: Amini appointed PM May 1961 under US Kennedy administration pressure; resigned July 1962. Confirmed.

events.title: Teachers Strike and Education Protests
events.note: 1961 teachers' strike confirmed; one teacher killed in Tehran clashes; contributed to US pressure for reform. Confirmed.

events.title: Land Reform Decree Issued
events.note: Land reform decree January 1962 precursor to White Revolution. Redistribution of large estates confirmed.

events.title: Women's Suffrage Piloted in Local Council Elections
events.note: Women granted local election vote/candidacy rights 1962; fierce clerical opposition documented. Formalized in 1963 referendum. Confirmed.

events.title: White Revolution Referendum
events.note: January 26, 1963 referendum; near-universal official approval; Khomeini condemned it as illegitimate. Confirmed.

events.title: June Uprising — Khomeini Arrested, Bloody Crackdown
events.note: Khomeini arrested June 5 (15 Khordad). Mass protests Tehran, Qom, Mashhad. Police files show 380 killed/wounded; regime tanks deployed. Confirmed. Description says 'June 3 arrest' but arrest was June 5; speeches were June 3 (Ashura). Minor date nuance; core event confirmed.

events.title: Khomeini Exiled for Opposing Status of Forces Agreement
events.note: Khomeini exiled November 1964 after SOFA sermon; went to Turkey then Najaf Iraq for 14 years. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Receives $200 Million US Loan Tied to SOFA
events.note: $200 million military loan linked to SOFA bill confirmed by multiple scholarly sources; Khomeini explicitly connected the two. Confirmed.

events.title: Prime Minister Hasan Ali Mansur Assassinated
events.note: Mansur shot January 21, 1965; died January 26. Assassin was Mohammad Bokharai of Islamic Coalition. Confirmed.

events.title: Amir Abbas Hoveyda Becomes Prime Minister
events.note: Hoveyda PM January 1965 to August 1977 (12 years, not 13 — minor discrepancy). Executed April 1979. Confirmed.

events.title: Oil Revenue Boom Funds Rapid Modernization
events.note: Mid-1960s oil revenue surge and Shah's industrialization/military expansion well documented. General contextual event confirmed.

events.title: Tehran Nuclear Research Reactor Goes Operational
events.note: 5 MW reactor became operational 1967; supplied by US under Atoms for Peace. Confirmed.

events.title: Formation of Mojahedin-e Khalq (MKO/MEK)
events.note: MKO founded 1965; became active in armed operations 1971 (not 1968). Description says 'founded 1965 and became active by 1968' which is approximately correct for founding phase. Year 1968 represents early armed activity. Confirmed with minor caveat.

events.title: Iran Signs Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
events.note: Iran signed NPT July 1, 1968; ratified February 2, 1970. Confirmed.

events.title: Khomeini Delivers Velayat-e Faqih Lectures in Najaf
events.note: Lectures delivered January-February 1969 at Najaf; later published as Islamic Government. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Abrogates 1937 Treaty on Shatt al-Arab
events.note: Iran unilaterally withdrew from 1937 treaty April 1969; demanded thalweg boundary. Led to Algiers 1975. Confirmed.

events.title: Fadayan-e Khalq Guerrilla Group Formed
events.note: Fadayan-e Khalq formally constituted as a merged group around 1971 (Siahkal operation February 1971). Year 1970 slightly early but founding period is correct. Confirmed with minor year note.

events.title: Iran Relinquishes Claim to Bahrain
events.note: UN survey 1970; Shah formally renounced claim; Bahrain independent August 1971. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Seizes Abu Musa and Greater and Lesser Tunbs Islands
events.note: November 30, 1971, eve of British withdrawal. Iranian seizure of all three islands confirmed. UAE never recognized Tunb sovereignty. Confirmed.

events.title: Nixon-Shah Agreement: Iran as Regional Policeman
events.note: Nixon visited Tehran May 1972; agreed Iran could buy any conventional weapons. Policy well documented in FRUS and declassified records. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Intervenes in Oman's Dhofar Rebellion
events.note: Iran deployed troops to Dhofar 1973-1976; decisive in ending rebellion. The event year 1972 is slightly early (deployment mainly 1973+). Core event confirmed; year is minor approximation.

events.title: Iran Benefits from OPEC Oil Embargo and Price Shock
events.note: Iran did not join Arab embargo but quadrupled oil revenues. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Assumes Full Control of Oil Industry from Consortium
events.note: Iran took operational control from consortium 1973; NIOC became direct manager. Confirmed.

events.title: Shah Announces Ambitious Nuclear Power Program
events.note: Shah announced 23-reactor plan 1974; contracts with Siemens/Framatome. US officials discussed weapons potential. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran's GDP Growth Surges on Oil Windfall
events.note: Iran's oil revenues rose ~5x in 1974; double-digit GDP growth; inflation and bottlenecks followed. Confirmed.

events.title: Rastakhiz: Single-Party State Imposed
events.note: Rastakhiz Party created March 1975; Shah dissolved all other parties; join or leave the country declaration confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Algiers Accord: Iran and Iraq Settle Border Dispute
events.note: Signed March 6, 1975; thalweg boundary for Shatt al-Arab; Iran ended Kurdish rebel support. Saddam repudiated it 1980. Confirmed.

events.title: International Condemnation of SAVAK Torture
events.note: Amnesty International 1976 reports on systematic SAVAK torture widely published; reached Carter campaign. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Changes Its Calendar to Imperial Calendar
events.note: Imperial calendar decree March 1976; year jumped from 1355 to 2535. Deeply unpopular; reversed after revolution. Confirmed.

events.title: Khomeini's Son Dies Suspiciously; Clergy Mobilizes
events.note: Mostafa Khomeini died October 23, 1977 in Najaf under suspicious circumstances; mourning processions became protests. Confirmed.

events.title: Carter Visits Tehran; Human Rights Dialogue Begins
events.note: Carter visited Tehran December 31, 1977; 'island of stability' toast confirmed in official records. Confirmed.

events.title: Revolutionary Year Begins: Cinema Rex Fire and Protests
events.note: Cinema Rex Abadan fire August 19, 1978; 377-430 killed (not 400 exactly); arson blamed on multiple parties. Confirmed.

events.title: Black Friday Massacre Accelerates Revolution
events.note: September 8, 1978 (Black Friday); firing on Jaleh Square protesters; official toll 84, opposition claims much higher. Confirmed.

events.title: Shah Leaves Iran; Islamic Revolution Triumphs
events.note: Shah left January 16, 1979; Khomeini returned February 1; armed forces declared neutrality February 11 — the official victory date. All dates confirmed.

events.title: Islamic Republic Referendum and New Constitution
events.note: March 30-31 1979 referendum; 98.2% for Islamic Republic. Constitution referendum December 1979. Confirmed.

events.title: US Embassy Hostage Crisis Begins
events.note: November 4, 1979; 66 hostages taken (52 held to end). Muslim Student Followers of Imam's Line. 444 days total. Khomeini endorsed. All dates confirmed.

events.title: Iran-Iraq War Begins
events.note: Iraqi invasion September 22, 1980; broad front attack; eight-year war; ~500,000 deaths. All key facts confirmed.

events.title: Failed US Hostage Rescue Mission — Operation Eagle Claw
events.note: April 24-25, 1980 (not April as stated). Eight servicemen killed at Desert One in helicopter/transport collision. Confirmed.

events.title: Hostages Released; Algiers Accords Signed
events.note: Accords signed January 19; hostages released January 20, 1981, minutes after Reagan inaugurated. 444 days. Confirmed.

events.title: Bombing of Islamic Republican Party Headquarters
events.note: June 28, 1981 bombing killed 72 including Beheshti. August 30 bombing killed President Rajai and PM Bahonar. All confirmed. MKO attributed.

events.title: Iran Recaptures Khorramshahr; War Turns
events.note: Operation Beit ol-Moqaddas; Khorramshahr recaptured May 24, 1982. Iran then invaded Iraq rather than negotiating. Confirmed.

events.title: Hezbollah Founded in Lebanon with Iranian Support
events.note: IRGC deployed to Bekaa Valley 1982 following Israeli invasion; trained and funded Hezbollah. Founding confirmed.

events.title: Suppression of the Tudeh Party
events.note: February 1983 arrests; Kianuri forced televised confession; hundreds imprisoned or executed. Confirmed.

events.title: War of the Cities and Tanker War Intensify
events.note: War of the Cities 1984-1988; Tanker War from 1984; Iraq targeted Gulf shipping. Confirmed.

events.title: Iraq Uses Chemical Weapons Against Iranian Forces
events.note: Iraq used mustard gas and nerve agents against Iran from 1983, major attacks 1984 (Majnoon Island) onward. UN-confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran-Contra Affair: Secret US Arms Sales to Iran
events.note: 1985-1986 Reagan administration secret arms sales to Iran despite embargo; proceeds diverted to Contras. Broke 1986. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Launches Human Wave Offensives with Child Soldiers
events.note: Basij human wave assaults including teenagers documented throughout 1983-1986; plastic 'keys to paradise' reported. Confirmed.

events.title: Faw Peninsula Captured by Iran
events.note: Operation Dawn 8; Faw Peninsula captured February 1986 in surprise amphibious assault. Confirmed.

events.title: US Navy Engages Iran in Persian Gulf
events.note: Operation Earnest Will (reflagged Kuwaiti tankers); October 1987 US attacked Iranian oil platforms (Operation Nimble Archer). Confirmed.

events.title: Mecca Pilgrimage Clashes Kill Over 400
events.note: July 31, 1987; 402 killed (275 Iranians, 85 Saudi security, 42 other pilgrims). Saudi embassy in Tehran attacked. Confirmed.

events.title: US Navy Shoots Down Iranian Civilian Airliner
events.note: July 3, 1988; USS Vincennes shot down Iran Air 655; 290 killed including 66 children. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Accepts UN Ceasefire; Khomeini Drinks 'Poison Chalice'
events.note: July 20, 1988 Khomeini accepted UNSCR 598. 'More deadly than taking poison' quote confirmed. Ceasefire August 20. Confirmed.

events.title: Mass Execution of Political Prisoners
events.note: Summer 1988 mass executions following Khomeini fatwa; primarily MKO and leftists. Estimates 1,400-5,000+. Amnesty/UN documented. Confirmed.

events.title: Khomeini Issues Fatwa Against Salman Rushdie
events.note: February 14, 1989 fatwa. Rushdie's 'The Satanic Verses.' EU ambassadors withdrawn. Multi-million dollar bounty. Confirmed.

events.title: Khomeini Dies; Khamenei Becomes Supreme Leader
events.note: Khomeini died June 3, 1989. Assembly of Experts elected Khamenei June 4 (60/86 votes); constitutional amendment removed Marja requirement July 1989. Confirmed.

events.title: Rafsanjani Becomes President; Era of Reconstruction Begins
events.note: Rafsanjani won presidential election July 28, 1989 (after constitutional reforms removed PM role). Confirmed.

events.title: Major Earthquake Devastates Northern Iran
events.note: June 21, 1990 Manjil-Rudbar earthquake; magnitude 7.4; 35,000-50,000 killed; 500,000 homeless. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Stays Neutral in Gulf Crisis; Benefits from Iraq's Weakening
events.note: Iran declared neutrality; Iraqi pilots flew aircraft to Iran; Iraq's military weakened. Confirmed.

events.title: Shapour Bakhtiar Assassinated in Paris
events.note: Bakhtiar assassinated August 6, 1991 in Suresnes (Paris suburb); Iranian agents convicted by French courts. Confirmed.

events.title: Mykonos Restaurant Assassinations
events.note: September 17, 1992; Kurdish opposition leaders killed in Berlin. German court 1997 found Khamenei and Rafsanjani committee ordered it. EU ambassadors withdrawn. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Acquires Nuclear Technology from Former Soviet States
events.note: Post-USSR collapse; Russia-Iran nuclear cooperation agreement 1992; Iranian acquisition of Soviet expertise confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: US Dual Containment Policy Targets Iran and Iraq
events.note: Clinton Dual Containment policy announced May 1993 (Martin Indyk). Both Iran and Iraq as rogue states. Confirmed.

events.title: Rafsanjani's Economic Liberalization Triggers Inflation and Unrest
events.note: Market liberalization and subsidy cuts caused inflation; Mashhad riots 1992, Qazvin 1994, Eslamshahr 1995. Confirmed.

events.title: Chain Murders of Intellectuals Begin
events.note: Chain murders 1988-1998 (main cluster mid-1990s); Mokhtari and Pouyandeh killed 1998. Description places start at 1994 which is approximately correct for the most visible cases. Confirmed.

events.title: US Comprehensive Sanctions on Iran Imposed
events.note: Clinton EO 12957 (March 1995) and EO 12959 (May 1995) banned US trade and investment in Iran. Confirmed.

events.title: Russia Signs Agreement to Complete Bushehr Nuclear Plant
events.note: Russia-Iran Bushehr agreement January 8, 1995. Completed 2011. US lobbied against. Confirmed.

events.title: D'Amato Act (ILSA): Third-Country Sanctions on Iran
events.note: ILSA signed August 5, 1996; $40 million investment threshold; extraterritorial reach resented by EU. Confirmed.

events.title: Khobar Towers Bombing; Iran Suspected
events.note: June 25, 1996; 19 USAF killed; 372 wounded. FBI found Saudi Hezbollah/Iran link. Confirmed.

events.title: Mohammad Khatami Wins Presidential Election in Landslide
events.note: May 23, 1997; Khatami won ~69% (not 70% exactly); ~80% turnout. Stunning upset. Confirmed. Minor: 69% not 70%.

events.title: Khatami Proposes Dialogue Among Civilizations
events.note: CNN interview January 1998; UN speech proposing dialogue vs Huntington clash thesis. Confirmed. (Year 1997 event; CNN interview was January 1998.)

events.title: Serial Murders Confession Shocks Iran
events.note: Ministry of Intelligence admitted 'rogue elements' responsible; late 1998 admission. Unprecedented. Confirmed.

events.title: Taliban Kills Iranian Diplomats; Tensions With Afghanistan
events.note: August 8, 1998; Taliban killed 11 Iranian diplomats + IRNA journalist in Mazar-i-Sharif. Iran massed 70,000+ troops on border. Confirmed.

events.title: Tehran University Student Uprising
events.note: July 8-13, 1999; Ansar-e Hezbollah attacked dormitories; largest protests since revolution; spread to multiple cities. Confirmed.

events.title: Reformist Press Flourishes Then Faces Closure Wave
events.note: Late 1990s reformist press surge; systematic judicial closures 1999-2000 documented by CPJ. Confirmed.

events.title: Reformists Win Majlis Elections; Guardian Council Resists
events.note: February 2000; reformists won ~195/290 seats. Guardian Council subsequently blocked legislation and disqualified future candidates. Confirmed.

events.title: US Secretary of State Albright Apologizes for 1953 Coup
events.note: March 17, 2000 Albright speech; acknowledged coup 'setback for Iran's political development.' Khamenei dismissed it. Confirmed.

events.title: Khatami Re-elected; Iran Cooperates After 9/11
events.note: Khatami re-elected June 8, 2001 with 77%. Iran-US Afghanistan cooperation post-9/11 confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Hosts Bonn Conference on Afghanistan's Post-Taliban Future
events.note: December 2001 Bonn Conference; Iran played constructive role supporting Karzai. US-Iranian direct cooperation noted. Confirmed.

events.title: Bush Labels Iran Part of 'Axis of Evil'
events.note: January 29, 2002 State of the Union; Iran, Iraq, North Korea. Enraged Iranian reformists who had cooperated post-9/11. Confirmed.

events.title: Nuclear Program Exposed: Natanz and Arak Facilities Revealed
events.note: NCRI press conference August 14, 2002 revealed Natanz enrichment and Arak heavy water sites. IAEA investigation triggered. Confirmed.

events.title: Bam Earthquake Kills 26,000
events.note: December 26, 2003; magnitude 6.6; 26,271 confirmed dead (official); Arg-e Bam citadel largely destroyed. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Signs Additional Protocol; Nuclear Negotiations Begin
events.note: Iran signed Additional Protocol December 18, 2003; EU-3 negotiations launched. Confirmed.

events.title: Guardian Council Disqualifies Reformist Candidates en Masse
events.note: January 2004; 3,600+ candidates disqualified including 80 sitting MPs. Khatami protest threats. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Temporarily Suspends Uranium Enrichment Under EU Deal
events.note: Paris Agreement November 2004; voluntary suspension of enrichment while negotiations continued. Ended 2005. Confirmed.

events.title: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad Elected President
events.note: June 2005 runoff; Ahmadinejad defeated Rafsanjani with ~62% vote. Confirmed.

events.title: Ahmadinejad Calls for Israel to Be 'Wiped Off the Map'
events.note: October 26, 2005 'World Without Zionism' conference. Quote and international response confirmed. Translation disputed by some scholars but the statement was made. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Resumes Uranium Enrichment; UN Sanctions Begin
events.note: Iran broke IAEA seals January 10, 2006; UNSCR 1737 passed December 2006. Confirmed.

events.title: Revolutionary Guard Designated Terrorist Organization by US
events.note: October 2007 EO 13382 designation of IRGC; Quds Force designated SDGT. First time component of foreign government military so designated. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Acknowledges 3,000 Centrifuges Operating at Natanz
events.note: Ahmadinejad announced 3,000 centrifuges September 2007. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Launches Domestically Built Satellite Rocket
events.note: Iran announced a rocket test February 2008 but the Safir rocket's first successful orbital launch was in February 2009. The 2008 test may have been a suborbital research rocket. Date/claim needs clarification — the orbital Safir launch was 2009, not 2008. Marking UNVERIFIED pending clarification.

events.title: Disputed Presidential Election and Green Movement
events.note: June 2009; official result 63% for Ahmadinejad disputed; Green Movement; violent crackdown; Mousavi and Karroubi eventually under house arrest. Confirmed.

events.title: Neda Agha-Soltan Shot Dead; Becomes Symbol of Green Movement
events.note: June 20, 2009; shot by Basij; video went viral globally; Time 100 most influential. Confirmed.

events.title: Stuxnet Cyber Weapon Attacks Iranian Nuclear Centrifuges
events.note: Stuxnet discovered 2010; US-Israeli joint operation; ~1,000 centrifuges destroyed; first industrial cyberweapon. Confirmed.

events.title: UN Security Council Imposes Toughest Sanctions Yet
events.note: UNSCR 1929 passed June 9, 2010; most comprehensive UN sanctions on Iran. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran's Influence Grows Amid Arab Spring
events.note: Iran's contradictory Arab Spring positioning (supporting Bahrain protesters, backing Assad against Syrian protesters) documented. Confirmed.

events.title: Crippling Oil Sanctions; Rial Collapses
events.note: 2012 US/EU oil and SWIFT sanctions; Iranian oil exports halved; rial lost 80%+ value; inflation 30%+. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Threatens to Close Strait of Hormuz
events.note: Iranian commanders repeatedly threatened Hormuz closure early 2012; US/UK naval response. Confirmed.

events.title: Hassan Rouhani Elected President on Moderate Platform
events.note: Rouhani won June 14, 2013 first-round with 50.7% (not 51% exactly). Moderate platform confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Rouhani and Obama Speak by Phone — First Leader Contact in 34 Years
events.note: September 27, 2013; 15-minute phone call confirmed; first US-Iran leader contact since 1979 revolution. Eggs thrown at Rouhani upon return confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Nuclear Talks Intensify Under Extended Deadlines
events.note: Multiple 2014 deadline extensions; P5+1 talks well documented. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Deepens Role in Iraq Amid ISIS Crisis
events.note: Iran first to send military advisers after ISIS seized Mosul June 2014; Soleimani directed operations. Confirmed.

events.title: JCPOA Nuclear Deal Signed
events.note: July 14, 2015 Vienna. Iran + P5+1 (US, UK, France, Russia, China) + Germany + EU. 97% uranium stockpile reduction. Date confirmed exactly.

events.title: Iran and Saudi Arabia Proxy War in Yemen Deepens
events.note: Saudi Operation Decisive Storm launched March 2015; Iran-Houthi support confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: JCPOA Implementation Day; Sanctions Relief
events.note: Implementation Day January 16, 2016; IAEA certified compliance; sanctions lifted; frozen assets released. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran-Saudi Arabia Break Diplomatic Relations
events.note: Nimr al-Nimr executed January 2, 2016; Saudi embassy attacked; Saudi Arabia cut ties January 3, 2016; Bahrain and Sudan followed. Confirmed.

events.title: Rouhani Re-elected; Economy and Social Freedoms Debated
events.note: Rouhani won May 19, 2017 with ~57% defeating Raisi. Unusually frank campaign confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: ISIS Attacks Tehran Parliament and Khomeini Shrine
events.note: June 7, 2017; simultaneous attacks on parliament and Khomeini mausoleum; 17 killed. First major ISIS attack inside Iran. Confirmed.

events.title: Trump Withdraws from JCPOA; Maximum Pressure Campaign
events.note: May 8, 2018; Trump announced withdrawal; maximum pressure campaign; all sanctions reimposed by November 5, 2018. Iran continued compliance ~1 year. Confirmed.

events.title: Nationwide Economic Protests Erupt Across 80 Cities
events.note: Protests began late December 2017 (not 2018); spread to 80+ cities; 25 killed, 3,700 arrested officially. Year label 2018 is slightly off — protests started Dec 28, 2017. Minor year discrepancy confirmed.

events.title: Gasoline Price Hike Sparks Nationwide Protests; Brutal Crackdown
events.note: November 15, 2019 gasoline price hike (50-200% depending on tier); protests within hours; Amnesty estimated 304+ killed; internet blackout ~1 week. Confirmed.

events.title: Attacks on Gulf Tankers and Saudi Aramco Facilities Attributed to Iran
events.note: 2019 Gulf tanker attacks attributed to Iran; Abqaiq September 14, 2019 knocked out ~5% global oil supply. Iran denied direct responsibility. Confirmed.

events.title: Qasem Soleimani Killed in US Drone Strike
events.note: January 3, 2020; Baghdad International Airport; US drone strike ordered by Trump. Iran declared national mourning; retaliated with missile strikes on US bases in Iraq. Confirmed.

events.title: Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 Shot Down
events.note: January 8, 2020; IRGC shot down PS752; 176 killed including 82 Iranian-Canadians. Iran initially denied then admitted. 'Death to the liar' protests followed. Confirmed.

events.title: Mohsen Fakhrizadeh, Nuclear Scientist, Assassinated
events.note: November 27, 2020 near Absard, Tehran Province; remote-controlled machine gun used. Israel blamed. Father of Iran's military nuclear program. Confirmed.

events.title: Ebrahim Raisi Elected President
events.note: June 18, 2021; Raisi won 62% in record-low 48.8% turnout after reformists disqualified. Confirmed.

events.title: JCPOA Negotiations Resume in Vienna
events.note: Vienna talks (indirect; Iran refused direct US talks) began April 2021; 8 rounds; near-complete draft 2022; IRGC designation stalled deal. Confirmed.

events.title: Mahsa Amini Dies; Woman Life Freedom Uprising and Crackdown
events.note: Mahsa (Zhina) Amini died September 16, 2022 after morality police arrest. 'Zan, Zendegi, Azadi' protests; 500+ killed; 20,000 arrested; 4+ protesters executed. Largest protests since 1979. UN confirmed violence caused death. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran and Saudi Arabia Restore Diplomatic Relations via China
events.note: March 10, 2023 Beijing agreement; embassies reopened May 2023; China-brokered. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Launches Direct Missile and Drone Attack on Israel
events.note: April 13-14, 2024 (Operation True Promise). 170 drones + 30 cruise missiles + 120 ballistic missiles = 320+ weapons. Israeli airstrike on Damascus consulate April 1 confirmed as trigger. 99% intercepted with US/UK/France/Jordan help. First direct Iran-Israel state attack. Confirmed.

events.title: President Raisi Dies in Helicopter Crash
events.note: May 19, 2024; Bell 212 crashed near Uzi village, East Azerbaijan in fog. Raisi + FM Amir-Abdollahian + 6 others killed. Dam inauguration with Aliyev confirmed. Mokhber became acting president. Confirmed.

events.title: Masoud Pezeshkian Elected President in Reformist Surprise
events.note: Runoff July 5, 2024; Pezeshkian won 53.7% (16.3M votes) vs Jalili 13.5M. Heart surgeon and moderate MP. Declared winner July 6. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran October 2024 Missile Strike on Israel
events.note: October 1, 2024 (Operation True Promise II); ~200 ballistic missiles in 2 waves; minor damage to Nevatim Airbase; 99% intercepted. Retaliation for assassinations of Haniyeh and Nasrallah. NOTE: This event is not in the curated JSON as a standalone entry — the curated file's 2024 entry only covers April 2024. The October strike is absent from the dataset.

events.title: Iran Advances Nuclear Program Toward Weapons-Grade Enrichment
events.note: IAEA confirmed 60% enrichment by early 2025; breakout time estimated under 2 weeks; inspection restrictions ongoing. Confirmed.

events.title: Trump Threatens Military Action; Diplomacy and Pressure Revive
events.note: Trump returned to office January 2025; reimposed maximum pressure; Oman-channel indirect talks resumed. Acute nuclear standoff confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Iran Deepens Strategic Partnership with Russia and China
events.note: Iran joined SCO as full member September 2023 (not 2025 as implied); strategic alignment with Russia and China deepened through 2025. Minor: SCO admission was 2023. Core trend confirmed.

flags: 2008 Satellite Rocket: Safir's first ORBITAL launch was February 2009, not 2008. The 2008 test was likely suborbital. Year/claim needs correction.
2018 Economic Protests: Protests started December 28, 2017. Year label 2018 is misleading.
October 2024 Iran-Israel missile strike (Operation True Promise II, Oct 1) is absent from the curated dataset — only the April 2024 attack is captured. Should be added as a separate event.
1965 Hoveyda PM tenure: 12 years (1965-1977), not 13 as stated.
